independent_review: Accepted within the bounded baseline scope

comparison.authority: The replay compares against the accepted current record. Earlier unavailable or unqualified records are not substituted.
comparison.frame_scope: Comparison includes the tag, declared length, payload and complete frame trailer. It is not limited to a selected projection.

verdict_semantics.Pass: Within the selected semantic reader's checked invariants, no violation is reported. This need not mean that the business operation succeeded; an expected publication failure can retain Pass.
verdict_semantics.Cancelled: The planned cut retains actual pending/completed knowledge without inventing returns, commit receipts, transfer or settlement.
verdict_semantics.invalid_scenario_scope: Rejected inputs retain no ownership facts.
verdict_semantics.raw_qualified_scope: The pinned adapter intentionally leaves qualified=false on every raw evaluation. Independent acceptance is recorded separately; the producer values are not promoted or rewritten.
verdict_semantics.FixtureMatched: The actual verdict equals the fixture's expected category. A match can be Pass, intentional Cancelled or InvalidScenario.

scope: The accepted result covers these 16 finite fixtures, their actual record/replay relation, complete observation streams and bounded execution cleanup.
The earlier same-execution before/after reader-copy checks retain their narrower scope. The current record and replay are distinct executions.
No new full ordinary-suite, compiler-build or binary-rebuild result is claimed by this comparison. Historical test results keep their original source and scope.
Portable tooling or metadata-fixture changes require their own validation; these accepted executions do not automatically qualify later packaging edits.
open_boundaries: Mutant detection, mutant replay, causal shrinking and four-role joins are not qualified by this baseline.
Full Stage4 acceptance remains open. Real PostgreSQL, network transport, clock and restart fidelity are not established by the fixture evidence.
Stage5 and Stage6 remain open; bounded cleanup does not prove all operating-system resource or fault boundaries.
The historical TLS timeout and earlier incomplete, unavailable, failed or held results retain their recorded status. The 72-hour soak remains cancelled.

parent_ci.scope: This is the existing public BOSH checkpoint. It is separate from the accepted baseline record/replay and does not establish CI for a later tooling or documentation checkpoint.

detailed_evidence: Complete results and retained historical stops are preserved separately. This public summary contains only the accepted scope, minimized outcomes and remaining boundaries.
